title: Tagging round skill
story: A member can now run a tagging round. The new /grillo-tagging skill gives every open ticket on GitHub one or more of the members' declared domains as labels, or the no-domain label, and it can be run again whenever someone joins. Tags a member set by hand are protected by a hidden marker comment, and deleting that comment hands the ticket back to the round. Before this, tickets stayed untagged after the grilling engine created them.

checks.criterion: /grillo-tagging gives every open ticket one or more declared domains, or domain:none, and creates any missing label
checks.steps: In a made-up test repository with a map, three open untagged tickets and a .grillo/members.json declaring product and developer on main, start claude in the clone. Type /grillo-tagging.
checks.expected: Every open ticket carries domain:product, domain:developer or domain:none on GitHub, and the missing labels exist. Closed tickets, kind labels, bodies and comments are unchanged, and the agent reports each ticket by title.

checks.criterion: The round never touches tags a member set by hand, which a <!-- grillo:tags-by-hand --> comment records
checks.steps: Ask the tagging agent to tag one ticket developer by hand, then check it posted the marker comment. Type /grillo-tagging again.
checks.expected: That ticket still carries only domain:developer, and the report lists it as left alone. After deleting its marker comment and running again, the round chooses its domains like any other ticket's.

checks.criterion: The round can be run again as members join
checks.steps: Add a made-up member to .grillo/members.json on main with a new domain such as workshop that fits a ticket now tagged domain:none. Type /grillo-tagging.
checks.expected: That ticket now carries domain:workshop instead of domain:none, and the other tickets keep sensible domains.
